record.original_question: In the setting of Theorem 5.1, let C be a class of infinite sequences of abelian groups, closed under isomorphism, such that there exist finitely presented groups G_1 and G_2 with the same first homology H_1(G_1) isomorphic to H_1(G_2), with H_*(G_1) in C and H_*(G_2) not in C. Theorem 5.1 proves that the set of finite presentations P for which the integral homology sequence H_*(P) belongs to C is not recursive. Under what additional hypotheses on C can this conclusion be strengthened by replacing 'not recursive' with 'not recursively enumerable'?

evidence.quote: Theorem 5.1. Let C be a class of infinite sequences (A1, A2, A3, . . .) of abelian groups which is closed under isomorphisms. Suppose there are finitely presented groups G1, G2 such that H1(G1) ∼= H1(G2), H∗(G1) ∈ C and H∗(G2) ∈ C /. Then the set of finite presentations P such that H∗(P) ∈ C is not recursive.
Question 5.2. When can one replace recursive by recursively enumerable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a class of infinite sequences $(A_1, A_2, A_3, \dots)$ of abelian groups that is closed under isomorphism (in the sense that if $(A_i) \in \mathcal{C}$ and $A_i \cong B_i$ for every $i$, then $(B_i) \in \mathcal{C}$). For a finite presentation $P = \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m angle$ of a group $G_P$, let $H_*(P) := (H_1(G_P; \mathbb{Z}), H_2(G_P; \mathbb{Z}), H_3(G_P; \mathbb{Z}), \dots)$ denote the integral homology sequence of $G_P$.

Assume that there exist finitely presented groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with $H_1(G_1) \cong H_1(G_2)$, $H_*(G_1) \in \mathcal{C}$, and $H_*(G_2) 
otin \mathcal{C}$. Under this hypothesis, the set
$$ \mathcal{S}(\mathcal{C}) := \{ P : P 	ext{ is a finite presentation and } H_*(P) \in \mathcal{C} \} $$
is known to be non-recursive (when finite presentations are encoded as natural numbers in any standard way).

Determine additional hypotheses on $\mathcal{C}$ under which one can strengthen this conclusion to: $\mathcal{S}(\mathcal{C})$ is not recursively enumerable. Equivalently, formulate sufficient conditions on $\mathcal{C}$ guaranteeing that no algorithm can enumerate the finite presentations $P$ with $H_*(P) \in \mathcal{C}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a published resolution of this question. The problem is posed as an open question in the source work on unsolvable problems about higher-dimensional knots and related groups, and no follow-up paper providing general sufficient conditions for non-r.e.-ness was identified.

status_evidence.title: Unsolvable problems about higher-dimensional knots and related groups
status_evidence.snippet: Section 5 shows that problems concerning computation of integral homology of finitely presented groups are unsolvable.
status_evidence.claim: The non-recursiveness theorem (Theorem 5.1) is established; replacing 'recursive' by 'recursively enumerable' is left as an open question.
